sessions.phase_label: Responsive landing-page delivery and website design-system planning
Website footer, access pages, and Admin Workspace design
Solution-page diagrams and continuing website refinement

requirements.title: Landing-Page Sign-Up Call to Action
requirements.definition: The initial landing page must provide a sign-up call to action that allows visitors to begin engaging with the service.
requirements.boundary_note: The sign-up action is independently required and can change without altering the page's broader visual direction or content structure.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Visual Direction
requirements.definition: The landing page must use the selected brand-aligned visual language, including its theme, typography roles, imagery treatment, accent usage, and logo treatment.
requirements.boundary_note: This covers the page-wide visual language; hero composition, content organization, responsive behavior, navigation, and footer behavior remain independently changeable Requirements.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Hero Presentation
requirements.definition: The landing-page hero must present the primary message and supporting visual in a clear, brand-aligned composition without overlap across supported layouts.
requirements.boundary_note: Hero emphasis, imagery, and layout can be revised or fail independently from the rest of the page's content sequence and general visual theme.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Content Structure
requirements.definition: The landing page must organize the approved copy into an appropriate single-page information sequence, including the post-hero How it Works section and its setup sequence.
requirements.boundary_note: This covers information architecture and approved page copy placement, not typography, responsive layout, navigation, or footer presentation.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Responsive Layout
requirements.definition: The landing page must provide usable and visually coherent layouts across desktop, tablet, mobile, and relevant intermediate viewport widths.
requirements.boundary_note: This is the implemented responsive behavior of the landing page; the reusable breakpoint rules for future pages are represented separately.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Build Stack
requirements.definition: The landing page must be implemented using the client-selected plain HTML and Tailwind CSS approach rather than Astro.
requirements.boundary_note: The selected implementation framework is independent from visual design decisions and from the delivery of design-system specifications.

requirements.title: Website Header Navigation
requirements.definition: The website must use the currently selected header-navigation behavior and menu structure for access to its pages and sections.
requirements.boundary_note: Header navigation has its own removal and later expansion trajectory, so it is separate from the page theme and footer.

requirements.title: Shared Website Footer
requirements.definition: Website pages must use a shared responsive footer containing the approved organization details, menu links, social links, copyright notice, and background treatment.
requirements.boundary_note: Footer content, responsive layout, links, and color treatment evolve together as one reusable component but independently from header navigation and page-level themes.

requirements.title: Shared Website Page Theme
requirements.definition: Follow-on website pages must carry forward a coherent brand theme, initially using the landing page's dark visual direction rather than a user-switchable color mode.
requirements.boundary_note: This governs page-level visual continuity; reusable header/footer components and specialized access-page styling have separate lifecycles.

requirements.title: Design Token Specification
requirements.definition: The website implementation must have an explicit token specification for colors and their uses, typography properties, spacing, radii, border widths, and related derived styling values.
requirements.boundary_note: The token definitions form one reusable design mechanism; binary font files, content-width selection, and responsive breakpoint guidance are independently deliverable.

requirements.title: Webfont Asset Delivery
requirements.definition: The implementation handoff must supply the required WOFF2 font files together with exact family names and the weights actually used.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a concrete asset-delivery obligation rather than the broader choice of typography values represented by the design-token Requirement.

requirements.title: Maximum Content Width
requirements.definition: The website design system must define a single confirmed maximum content width for consistent container sizing.
requirements.boundary_note: The container cap is an independently consumable layout rule and can change without replacing the broader token sheet.

requirements.title: Responsive Breakpoint Guidance
requirements.definition: The website design system must provide reusable guidance or rules for responsive breakpoints and general viewport behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: This defines reusable responsive rules for future pages, while landing-page-specific responsive implementation is a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Informational Page Shell
requirements.definition: Informational and non-marketing pages must use a minimal branded shell with an appropriate background, header logo, and applicable shared footer.
requirements.boundary_note: This is the reusable shell shared across non-marketing pages; Cognito sign-in styling and provisioning-wizard controls remain specialized Requirements.

requirements.title: Cognito Sign-In Branding
requirements.definition: The AWS Cognito-generated sign-in experience must be customized with LumenArc branding and an approved sign-in background treatment.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement concerns visual customization of the generated authentication page, not the underlying authentication functionality or general informational-page shell.

requirements.title: Provisioning Wizard Styling
requirements.definition: The account or tenant provisioning wizard must use approved typography, active-node accents, surfaces, dimensions, gaps, and interactive button states across portrait and landscape layouts.
requirements.boundary_note: Wizard-specific progress, panel, and control styling can evolve independently from the sign-in page and the shared minimal page shell.

requirements.title: Policy Document Access
requirements.definition: Standard policy destinations such as Cookie Notice and Privacy Policy must be accessible using the currently selected temporary PDF-in-new-tab behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: The temporary delivery behavior of policy content is independently changeable and should not be folded into footer layout merely because footer links expose it.

requirements.title: Additional Page Prototype Code
requirements.definition: Provide optional rough implementation code for the additional access and provisioning pages as a concrete handoff artifact.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a task-local coding deliverable distinct from the persistent visual and behavioral specifications of the pages themselves.

requirements.title: Admin Workspace Shell Styling
requirements.definition: The Admin Workspace shell must have brand-aligned styling for its header, side navigation, footer, shell container, and canvas in both light and dark themes, without expanding into inner application-screen design.
requirements.boundary_note: This covers the shell's overall look and component styling while excluding independently evolving application screens, panel architecture, and button-system decisions.

requirements.title: Admin Workspace Panel Navigation
requirements.definition: The Admin Workspace must use a coherent collapsible navigation-panel structure that avoids visually competing shell and application panels and supports access to application-specific items.
requirements.boundary_note: Panel placement and nesting are independently testable interaction decisions rather than attributes of the shell's general colors and typography.

requirements.title: Admin Workspace Button Styling
requirements.definition: Admin Workspace buttons must use a consistent approved treatment for color, shape, size, rounding, and optional icon usage.
requirements.boundary_note: The button system can be modified without changing the rest of the Admin Workspace shell and therefore warrants a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Omnichannel Interaction Diagram
requirements.definition: Produce a production-ready website diagram showing customer and staff interaction channels with the approved phone, email, message, chat, and report labels.
requirements.boundary_note: This diagram has its own content labels and acceptance criteria and can be revised independently from the separate cyclic-process diagram.

requirements.title: Cyclic Process Diagram
requirements.definition: Produce a production-ready website diagram whose process cycle uses clockwise directional arrows.
requirements.boundary_note: The cyclic diagram has a distinct structure and directional-arrow requirement, so it should not be represented merely as an attribute of the interaction diagram.

unresolved_candidates.description: The freelancer proposed a landing-page contact form and explicitly asked whether it should be retained or removed, but no client decision establishing it as an independent Requirement is visible.
Pricing presentation remains unresolved: the freelancer asked whether to show pricing directly or use a contact-for-pricing prompt, but no authoritative client choice is visible.
The client switched background assets to JPEG for size reduction, but it is unclear whether this is a durable independent asset-format Requirement or only an incidental implementation note.
